mainTopic: The retroactive impurity of a woman who sees blood (מעת לעת) or a stain (כתם), and רב הונא's rule that it applies to קודש but not to תרומה
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבא's statement: during the מעת לעת window, a woman's bed and seat are as strong as her own touch, making a person impure along with his clothes. A ברייתא is brought that fits רבא. It compares a woman who sees blood with a woman who finds a כתם: what each makes impure retroactively, whether her count is thrown off, and whether the man who was with her becomes impure, where רבי עקיבא disagrees. In both cases, תרומה she touched is left in doubt, neither eaten nor burned. The גמרא asks why רבא needed a קל וחומר if he knew the ברייתא, and answers that the ברייתא alone does not show how strong the impurity is. Then רב הונא rules that מעת לעת applies only to קודש, not to תרומה. His rule survives challenges from the list of מעלות, from the ברייתא's 'food and drink,' and from רבי יהודה's required check after eating תרומה. The amud ends as a new challenge begins from a story where רבי ruled like רבי אליעזר; it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Her bed and seat are like her own touch
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his statement: during the retroactive period, her משכב and מושב are like her own touch. They make a person impure to the point that he makes his clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Her bed and seat] are like her own touch. Her touch makes a person impure, so much that he then makes his clothes impure. In the same way, her bed and her seat make a person impure, so much that he makes his clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבא's statement. The bed and seat a woman used during the retroactive period carry the same strong impurity as touching her directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how strong the retroactive impurity of her bed and seat is. רבא compares them to her own touch. That touch makes a person impure even for his clothes, so the bed and seat do the same. Retroactive impurity here is not a weaker kind of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Her own touch: someone directly touching the woman herself
A bed or anything made for lying on, which a נדה makes impure
A seat or anything made for sitting on, which a נדה makes impure
Makes a person impure strongly enough that he also makes the clothes he is wearing impure

phrases.english: are like her own touch.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבא's sentence. The words 'her bed and her seat' came just before, at the bottom of the previous page.

phrases.english: Just as her own touch makes a person impure
to the point that he makes clothes impure,
so too her bed and her seat make a person impure
to the point that he makes clothes impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַגַּע עַצְמָהּ, מָה מַגַּע עַצְמָהּ מְטַמֵּא אָדָם לְטַמֵּא בְּגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's statement, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the retroactive period, her bed and seat are as strong as her own touch: they make a person impure along with his clothes.

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits רבא: a woman who sees blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבא. A woman who sees blood is impure retroactively for מעת לעת. She makes beds, seats, food, drink and a sealed clay vessel impure. But her count of days is not thrown off, and a man who was with her is not made impure retroactively.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits רבא: A woman who sees blood is impure going back twenty-four hours. What does she make impure? Beds and seats, food and drink, and a clay vessel sealed with a tight cover. But her count is not thrown off, and she does not make the man who was with her impure retroactively.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבא. It lists beds and seats among the things a woman makes impure during the twenty-four hours before she saw blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats beds and seats as really impure during the retroactive period, which fits רבא's view. It also sets limits on how far the retroactive impurity reaches. It does not disturb her counting of days, and it does not reach a man who was with her.

keyTerms.meaning: A twenty-four-hour period, counted backward from when she saw blood
A tightly sealed cover on a clay vessel, which normally protects it from impurity
Her count of days is thrown off
The man who was intimate with her
Retroactively, going back in time

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up a side-by-side comparison between seeing blood and finding a stain. The rest of this section depends on that comparison.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבא:
A woman who sees blood is impure going back twenty-four hours,
And what does she make impure?
Beds and seats, food and drink,
and a clay vessel sealed with a tight cover,
phrases.notes: Touching a sealed clay vessel can't make it impure, but a נדה makes it impure by moving it.

phrases.english: but her count is not thrown off,
phrases.notes: Her cycle of days is counted from when she actually saw the blood, not from the earlier twenty-four hours.

phrases.english: and she does not make the man who was with her impure retroactively.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's statement
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that her bed and seat are impure during the retroactive period
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists משכבות ומושבות among the things a woman who sees blood makes impure מעת לעת

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the man who was with her is impure too
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. In his view, a woman who sees blood does make the man who was with her impure. She counts her days only from the time she saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: She does make the man who was with her impure. And she counts only from the time she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא disagrees with the first opinion about the man who was with her during the twenty-four hours. He says that man is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the retroactive impurity does not reach the man. רבי עקיבא extends it to him. Even so, her own seven days are counted from when she actually saw the blood, not from earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: She counts her days of impurity
From the moment she actually saw the blood

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up two different things. The impurity she spreads to objects (and, for רבי עקיבא, to the man) goes back in time. But the count of her own seven days starts only from when she saw.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מְטַמֵּא אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ,
phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: She makes the man who was with her impure,
and she counts only from the time that she saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מְטַמֵּא אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who sees blood makes the man who was with her impure retroactively. Her own count still starts from when she saw.

steps.title: A woman who finds a stain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא moves on to a woman who finds a כתם. She is impure retroactively and makes the same things impure. Unlike seeing blood, the stain throws off her count, and she makes the man who was with her impure. She still counts only from when she saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who sees a stain is impure retroactively. What does she make impure? Food and drink, beds and seats, and a clay vessel sealed with a tight cover. Her count is thrown off, and she makes the man who was with her impure. And she counts only from the time she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the rules for a woman who finds a blood stain, to compare with a woman who sees actual blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a stain, the impurity is not measured as twenty-four hours. It goes back to the last time the garment was checked. Two rules are stricter than with seeing blood. Her count is thrown off, and the man who was with her becomes impure. The objects she makes impure are the same list as before.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment or body, without seeing when it came out

steps.whatToRemember: Seeing blood: impure for twenty-four hours back, count not thrown off, man not impure (except for רבי עקיבא). Finding a stain: impure going back, count thrown off, man impure. In both cases her own count starts from when she saw.

phrases.english: A woman who sees a stain is impure retroactively,
phrases.notes: Here 'retroactively' means back to the last time the garment was checked, not just twenty-four hours.

phrases.english: And what does she make impure?
Food and drink, beds and seats,
and a clay vessel sealed with a tight cover,
and her count is thrown off,
phrases.notes: Since nobody knows when the stain came, she can't be sure where she is in her count of days.

phrases.english: and she makes the man who was with her impure,
and she counts only from the time that she saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the case of a stain, to compare with seeing blood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who finds a stain is impure retroactively. Her count is thrown off and she makes the man who was with her impure, but she counts her days from when she saw.

steps.title: In both cases, the תרומה is left in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that in both cases, the woman who saw blood and the woman who found a stain, the תרומה she touched is left in doubt. It is not eaten and not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both this case and that case, we leave it hanging: we don't eat it and we don't burn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with a rule that covers both cases: food that is in doubt because of the retroactive impurity is set aside, neither eaten nor burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The retroactive impurity is only a doubt, so the food can't be treated as certainly impure or certainly pure. Eating it is forbidden in case it is impure. Burning it, which is what you do with impure תרומה, is also forbidden in case it is pure. So it is left aside.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that: here, both the woman who saw blood and the woman who found a stain
We leave it hanging: the food's status stays undecided
We burn it, as is done with תרומה that is definitely impure

steps.whatToRemember: Retroactive impurity is only a doubt. That is why the food is neither eaten nor burned.

phrases.english: And in both this case and that case, we leave it hanging,
phrases.notes: This is about תרומה she touched during that earlier stretch of time.

phrases.english: we do not eat it and we do not burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא with a rule that applies to both cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In both cases, תרומה touched during the retroactive period is left in doubt: not eaten and not burned.

steps.title: Why did רבא need a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: either רבא knew the ברייתא, so he should just quote it, or he didn't, so where did he get the base for his קל וחומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: As for רבא: if he knew the ברייתא, let him just quote it. If he didn't know it, where did he get his קל וחומר from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבא proved his rule. It sets up a two-sided trap: either way, his method looks strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's קל וחומר was built on the rule of the sealed clay vessel, and that rule comes from the ברייתא. But the same ברייתא also says beds and seats become impure. So if he knew it, the proof was already there. If he didn't, he had no base for his קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Here, the ברייתא quoted earlier
He heard it / he knew of it
From where does he get it?

phrases.english: And Rava: if he heard the baraita —
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 2, the one that lists both the clay vessel and beds and seats.

phrases.english: let him say the baraita!
And if he did not hear the baraita —
from where does he have the kal vachomer?
phrases.notes: His קל וחומר started from the sealed clay vessel rule, which he could only know from that ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבא's statement after the ברייתא has been fully quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice to use a קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either the ברייתא makes the קל וחומר unnecessary, or without the ברייתא the קל וחומר has no starting point

steps.title: The ברייתא alone could be read more weakly
steps.stepSummary: רבא did know the ברייתא, but from it alone one might think beds and seats make a person or clothes impure, not a person who then makes his clothes impure. So he needed the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did know the ברייתא. But from the ברייתא alone I would have said that beds and seats make impure either a person or clothes, but not a person and also his clothes. That is why he said the קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבא knew the ברייתא, but it does not prove the full strength of his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says her beds and seats are impure. It does not say how strong that impurity is. רבא's קל וחומר adds that it is strong enough to make a person impure to the point that he makes his clothes impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (opens an answer that keeps the original assumption)
I would have thought
Because of this / that is why

steps.whatToRemember: רבא used the ברייתא as his starting point, but his קל וחומר shows that her beds and seats carry a stronger impurity than the ברייתא alone shows.

phrases.english: Actually, he did hear the baraita,
but if it were only from the baraita, I would have said:
either a person or clothes,
phrases.notes: He means the bed makes impure a person or clothes that touch it.

phrases.english: but a person and his clothes — no.
phrases.notes: The person would not become impure enough to pass the impurity on to the clothes he is wearing.

phrases.english: That is why he says the kal vachomer.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the source is weaker than assumed, so the extra proof is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the ברייתא alone: her bed makes a person or clothes impure, but not a person to the point of making his clothes impure
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר teaches the stronger level, as רבא said

steps.title: רב הונא: מעת לעת applies only to קודש
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the backward-looking twenty-four-hour impurity of a נדה applies to קודש but not to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The מעת לעת impurity of a נדה applies to קודש, but not to תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא limits the backward-looking impurity to holy foods only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a woman who sees blood is impure for the past twenty-four hours. רב הונא says this only matters for קודש. תרומה she touched during that time is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: A twenty-four-hour period, here counted backward from when she saw blood
Holy food, such as meat of קרבנות
The portion of produce given to a כהן; holy, but less strict than קודש

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The twenty-four-hour period of a niddah is for sacred food,
but not for terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מֵעֵת לְעֵת שֶׁבְּנִדָּה לַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the scope of the מעת לעת impurity
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעת לעת of a נדה applies to קודש, not to תרומה

steps.title: Then it should be in the list of stringencies
steps.stepSummary: If this rule is only for קודש, it should appear in the list of extra stringencies that apply to קודש and not to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it be taught among the list of extra stringencies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. If his rule is true, why is it missing from the known list?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a list (in חגיגה) of purity rules that are stricter for קודש than for תרומה. רב הונא's rule is exactly that kind of difference. So it is odd that the list leaves it out.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Extra stringencies of purity that apply to קודש beyond תרומה

phrases.english: If so, let it be taught among the "levels"!
phrases.notes: This is the list in מסכת חגיגה of purity rules that are stricter for קודש than for תרומה.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A difference between קודש and תרומה should appear in the list of מעלות, but it doesn't

steps.title: The list only includes cases with a real basis in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The list of מעלות only includes cases that have a basis in real impurity. מעת לעת has no such basis, so it is not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that list teaches cases, it is where there is a basis of impurity. Where there is no basis of impurity, it does not list it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what kind of cases the list includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מעלות list only covers cases that have some connection to impurity on the level of Torah law. The backward-looking מעת לעת impurity is only a rabbinic rule with no such Torah-level connection. So leaving it off the list does not disprove רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A basis or connection to real impurity
It teaches / it lists

phrases.english: When it teaches,
it is where there is a basis of impurity,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ דְּרָרָא דְּטוּמְאָה — לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: but where there is no basis of impurity, it does not teach it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי הֵיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ דְּרָרָא דְּטוּמְאָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the list being cited
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every difference between קודש and תרומה should be in the list of מעלות
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only includes cases with a basis in real impurity; מעת לעת has none

steps.title: The ברייתא says she makes food and drink impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from the ברייתא: she makes food and drink impure. Doesn't that mean both קודש and תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: What does she make impure? Food and drink. Doesn't that mean both קודש and תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to רב הונא, this time from the ברייתא about the woman who sees blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says food and drink become impure during the מעת לעת and does not limit it. Plain reading suggests all food, including תרומה. That would go against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Food and drink
Isn't it so that…? (a leading question that pushes a reading)

phrases.english: They challenged:
What does she make impure? Food and drink.
phrases.notes: This is from the ברייתא in step 2 about her retroactive impurity.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, בֵּין דְּקֹדֶשׁ בֵּין דִּתְרוּמָה?
phrases.english: Is it not both of sacred food and of terumah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מָה הִיא מְטַמְּאָה? אֳוכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב הונא after the first one was answered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says food and drink without limiting it, which seems to include תרומה

steps.title: The ברייתא means only קודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the food and drink in the ברייתא are only קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means food and drink of קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא narrowly, so it fits רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say which food it means. The גמרא reads it as talking only about קודש. That way the ברייתא does not contradict רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Of קודש (holy food)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives two challenges: the מעלות list leaves out cases with no basis in real impurity, and the ברייתא's food and drink means only קודש.

phrases.english: No, of sacred food.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's food and drink means both קודש and תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's food and drink means only קודש

steps.title: A new challenge from רבי יהודה's ruling on checking after eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה's ruling that women must check themselves even after eating תרומה. It also recalls the old question: what good is a check after the eating is already over?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says that women must check themselves even when they finish eating תרומה. And we discussed this ruling and asked: what happened, happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רב הונא. It quotes רבי יהודה's ruling and the earlier question about it, so that the next line can explain what the check is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה requires a check after eating תרומה. The question is obvious: if she was impure while eating, the eating is already done, so what can the check fix? The answer, which comes next, is what will create the problem for רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: When they finish (eating)
And we discussed it (an earlier discussion is being recalled)
What happened, happened. The past cannot be changed

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda says,
even at the time they finish
phrases.notes: This is about women from כהן families, who check themselves before eating תרומה. רבי יהודה adds a check afterward too.

phrases.english: eating תרומה (they must check).
And we discussed it:
What happened, happened!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף בִּשְׁעַת עֲבָרָתָן מִלֶּאֱכוֹל בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 12, the גמרא brings a new source to test רב הונא's rule again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that מעת לעת does not apply to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A required check after eating תרומה hints that her later impurity might matter for תרומה. The full force of this comes with רב חסדא's explanation.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the check protects the leftover תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the check is needed to protect the leftover תרומה in front of her. This suggests her impurity can reach back and affect תרומה, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It was only needed to take care of the leftovers that are in front of her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question of 'what happened, happened.' His answer is what makes this a real challenge to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, the check keeps the leftover תרומה from becoming impure through a backward-looking impurity. That only makes sense if מעת לעת does apply to תרומה. That is exactly what רב הונא said it does not do.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for
To fix or take care of (here: to protect)
Leftovers, the remaining food

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It was needed only
to take care of the leftovers that are in front of her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְתַקֵּן שִׁירַיִם שֶׁבְּפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 13, and that answer turns into a challenge against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that the backward-looking impurity does not reach תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a check is needed to protect leftover תרומה, then backward-looking impurity must be able to affect תרומה.

steps.title: רב הונא's version: the check decides whether to burn the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches the ruling differently. The check decides whether the leftover תרומה must be burned, and this applies only when she checked right after eating, within the short time of a וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא teaches: to burn the leftovers that are in her hands, in a case where she checked herself within the time-span of a וסת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge by teaching the purpose of the check differently. In his version, there is no backward-looking impurity at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she checks right away, within the tiny time-span of a וסת, and finds blood, it counts as if she saw blood while eating. Then she was surely impure, and the leftover תרומה is definitely impure and must be burned. That is regular, present impurity, not מעת לעת, so רב הונא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches (a version of the ruling)
To burn. Definitely impure תרומה is burned
Within the short time-span of a menstrual onset

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying her impurity reaches back twenty-four hours for תרומה. He is talking about a check done right away, which shows she was impure at that very time.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב הונא, the leftover תרומה is burned only when an immediate check proves she was impure while eating. מעת לעת still does not apply to תרומה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna teaches
to burn the leftovers that are in her hands,
where she checked herself
within the time-span of a וסת.
phrases.notes: A very short moment right after eating. So if she finds blood, she was surely impure while she ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא מַתְנֵי לִישְׂרוֹף שִׁירַיִם שֶׁבְּיָדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב חסדא's explanation in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the ruling: the purpose of the check is changed to fit רב הונא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The check protects leftover תרומה from backward-looking impurity, so מעת לעת applies to תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The check only decides whether to burn the leftovers when an immediate check proves she was surely impure. That is not מעת לעת.

steps.title: Another challenge: רבי acted like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story in which רבי ruled in practice like רבי אליעזר. This opens another challenge to רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There was an incident, and רבי acted according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next challenge to רב הונא. It only begins the story here; how this story goes against רב הונא is explained on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מעשה is a real case where a ruling was put into practice, so it carries strong weight. רבי followed רבי אליעזר's opinion about a woman's backward-looking impurity, and the גמרא will look at what that ruling shows about רב הונא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case decided in practice
And he acted according to (he ruled in practice like)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There was an incident,
and רבי acted according to Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא. Why this story matters for רב הונא comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַעֲשֶׂה, וְעָשָׂה רַבִּי כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא's answer in step 15, the גמרא opens a fresh challenge from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that מעת לעת does not apply to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story of רבי ruling like רבי אליעזר is brought as a source that may go against רב הונא. The details are explained on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי says רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on
steps.stepSummary: After he remembered that רבי אליעזר's view was disputed, רבי said that רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רבי remembered, he said: רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story of רבי from the last step. This line prepares the challenge to רב הונא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי had already ruled like רבי אליעזר. Then he remembered that other Sages argue with רבי אליעזר. He still did not take back the ruling, because he felt רבי אליעזר's opinion is strong enough to lean on.

keyTerms.meaning: He remembered
Worthy, deserving
To rely on him, to follow his ruling

phrases.english: After he remembered,
phrases.notes: He remembered that the other Sages disagree with רבי אליעזר, so his ruling seemed to follow a minority view.

phrases.english: he said: רבי אליעזר is worthy
to rely upon him

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּזְכַּר, אָמַר: כְּדַי הוּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story about רבי that step 16 began. The sentence and the challenge to רב הונא built on it continue on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after remembering that other Sages disagree, רבי held that רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on.
